memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Early the next morning Joshua had Israel come forward by tribes, and Judah was chosen. The clans of Judah came forward, and he chose the Zerahites. He had the clan of the Zerahites come forward by families, and Zimri was chosen. Joshua had his family come forward man by man, and Achan son of Karmi, the son of Zimri, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was chosen. — Josh 7:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The searching process unfolds exactly as God said. Tribe by tribe, the circle narrows — Judah, then the Zerahites, then Zimri's family, and finally one man: Achan. Imagine the tension of that morning. With each step, the circle grows smaller and the guilty man's hiding place grows tighter, until at last he stands exposed before all Israel.

Think of what Achan endured through this. He knew he was guilty. As the lot drew nearer, tribe by tribe, clan by clan, he could have stepped forward at any moment and confessed. Instead he stayed silent, hoping perhaps that he would not be caught, that his secret would hold. But sin has a way of being found out. "Be sure that your sin will find you out" (Num 32:23).

This slow narrowing was actually a mercy — a lengthy, unmistakable call to confess. God was giving Achan every chance to come clean before he was named. How much better it would have been for Achan to step out early and admit his guilt. How much better it always is for us to confess quickly rather than wait to be exposed.

There is a searching truth here for all of us. We cannot ultimately hide from God. What we conceal will one day come into the light. But the good news is that we do not have to wait to be caught. We can come to God now, freely confessing, and find that in Christ there is cleansing rather than exposure and shame (Prov 28:13). The One who searches us out is also the One who longs to forgive.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you waiting to be "caught" rather than confessing something to God now?
2. How does knowing sin will be found out encourage you toward honesty?
3. Why is it always better to come clean quickly rather than hide and hope?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I would rather confess to You now than be exposed later. Give me an honest heart that comes quickly into Your light, where I find forgiveness in Christ. Amen.
